policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Article on the proper name only; ASV 'Mary the mother of James' renders the name identically whether or not the Greek article stands, and no note is mapped here (the 'Or, Jacob' note is an alternative_rendering of Ἰακώβου).

Article plus genitive article versus their omission; ASV 'Mary the mother of James' identifies her by the same genitive relation either way, and the supplied 'the mother of' is an English idiom for the bare genitive, not a witness to ἡ τοῦ.
All three readings are the ordinary Greek idiom for the first day of the week; ASV 'on the first day of the week' renders any of them without distinguishing article or case.
ἐκ and ἀπὸ are both rendered 'from' before τῆς θύρας; ASV 'from the door of the tomb' does not distinguish the prepositions.

ἀποκυλίω and ἀνακυλίω both denote rolling the stone off the entrance and are both idiomatically Englished 'rolled back'; ASV's 'roll us away' in v. 3 for a different clause is stylistic variation and no mapped note stands here.
ASV renders the clause causally, 'for trembling and astonishment had come upon them', which is γάρ; the RP δέ would be the continuative 'and'.

ASV prints vv. 9-20 as text of the Gospel (they are rendered in full below) and relegates both the omission and the other ending to the margin: 'The two oldest Greek manuscripts, and some other authorities, omit from verse 9 to the end. Some other authorities have a different ending to the Gospel.' So the long ending stands in the text and the intermediate ending does not.
παρ᾽ ἧς and ἀφ᾽ ἧς are alike rendered 'from whom'; ASV 'from whom he had cast out seven demons' does not distinguish them, and the mapped note concerns the presence of vv. 9-20, not this preposition.
ASV 'And afterward he was manifested' supplies a connective; the RP omission leaves ὕστερον asyndetic, which ASV would render 'Afterward' without 'And'.
ASV ends the verse 'after he was risen', with nothing answering to ἐκ νεκρῶν ('from the dead'), which it renders explicitly wherever it stands.
ASV 'these signs shall accompany them that believe' renders the compound παρακολουθήσει; it reserves 'follow' for ἀκολουθέω and its cognates, as at v. 20 'the signs that followed'.
ASV reads 'they shall speak with new tongues' in the text and marks the omission as the variant: 'Some ancient authorities omit new' (textual_variant), so καιναῖς stands.
ASV 'they shall take up serpents' has nothing answering to καὶ ἐν ταῖς χερσίν ('and in their hands'), which the longer reading would require.
ASV 'So then the Lord Jesus' renders Ἰησοῦς explicitly; the RP omission gives only 'the Lord'.
ASV closes the Gospel 'by the signs that followed. Amen.', rendering the added Ἀμήν in the text.
